extracted.intended_audience: NIH/AHRQ fellowship applicants, sponsors/co-sponsors, reference letter writers, and peer reviewers (F30, F31, F32, F33, F99/K00)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and peer-reviewing NIH and AHRQ fellowship (NRSA-style) applications, detailing the revised scored review criteria and corresponding changes to the PHS Fellowship Supplemental Form effective for due dates on or after Jan 25, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate's Preparedness and Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the candidate's preparedness for the proposed research training plan and consider context (e.g., stage of training, opportunities available). Assess whether candidate and sponsor statements and referee letters provide convincing evidence that the candidate possesses qualities (such as scientific understanding, creativity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and drive) that will improve likelihood of a successful research training outcome. Consider the candidate's potential to benefit from the fellowship research training plan and to transition to the next career stage in the biomedical research workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus reviewer attention on the candidate's demonstrated and potential attributes rather than institutional or sponsor prestige; consider context of opportunities and stage of training; use candidate/sponsor statements and reference letters to judge qualities and likelihood to benefit and transition to next career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the rigor and feasibility of the research training project and how completion of the project will contribute to the development of the candidate as a research scientist. Evaluate the goals of the overall research training plan and the extent to which the plan will facilitate attainment of those goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review whether the plan identifies areas of needed development and contains appropriate, realistic activities and milestones to address those needs. Consider whether sponsor(s), scientific environment, facilities, and resources are adequate and appropriate for the proposed research training plan. Emphasize training-related headings in the application (Training Activities and Timeline; Specific Aims; Strategy including Scientific Foundation & Rationale and Approach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the sponsor(s) presents a strong mentoring plan appropriate to the needs and goals of the candidate. Evaluate the extent to which the sponsor(s) and organizational commitment is appropriate, sufficient, and in alignment with the candidate's research training plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the level of commitment provided will contribute to successful completion of the proposed plan and allow the candidate to advance to a productive career in the biomedical research workforce. Avoid undue weight on sponsor or institutional reputation; focus on tangible mentoring plans and organizational support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers' Focus and Bias Reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review should better focus reviewer attention on three key assessments: the fellowship candidate's preparedness and potential, the research training plan, and commitment to the candidate. Reduce bias by emphasizing commitment to the candidate without undue consideration of sponsor and institutional reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify and simplify language in application and review criteria so a broad range of candidates and research training contexts can be recognized as meritorious. Reviewers should weigh evidence in statements and letters and consider contextual factors (training stage, opportunities) to mitigate reputational or institutional bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of Grades from Candidate Section
rubrics_metrics.description: Grades will no longer be required or allowed in the Applicant (now Candidate) Section of the PHS Fellowship Supplemental Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not include grades; applications and reviewers will not use grades as an indicator. Update submissions to omit any grade information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Candidate Personal Statements (four)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates are required to submit four personal statements: (1) a statement of professional and fellowship goals, (2) fellowship qualifications, (3) a self-assessment, and (4) scientific perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each statement should address the named topic and provide information reviewers need to evaluate preparedness, potential, and fit with the research training plan. The self-assessment and scientific perspective should help contextualize the candidate's background and trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Plan Section Structure and Headings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Training Plan section headings have been revised to emphasize training. The sections include: (1) Training Activities and Timeline, (2) Research Training Project Specific Aims, (3) Research Training Project Strategy, including the Scientific Foundation & Rationale and Approach. The previous 'Selection of Sponsor and Institution' section has been removed and that information is to be included elsewhere in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should structure the Research Training Plan with clear aims, explicit training activities and milestones, and an articulated scientific foundation and approach; emphasize how training elements address identified developmental needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor and Co-sponsor Statements (Commitment to Candidate, Mentoring, and Training Environment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors and co-sponsors must submit five statements: (1) Mentoring Approach and Candidate Mentoring Plan; (2) Prior Commitment to Training and Mentoring; (3) Commitment to the Candidate's Research Training Plan; (4) Research Training Environment; and (5) Candidate's Potential. A sixth statement on Clinical Training is required for candidates proposing to gain experience in a clinical trial as part of the research training plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor statements should provide concrete plans and evidence of prior mentoring commitment, alignment with the candidate's goals, and details about the training environment and resources. For clinical-trial-related training, include the Clinical Training statement. Reviewers will assess these statements under the 'Commitment to Candidate' criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Letter Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH and AHRQ will provide detailed instructions for reference letters so they better assist reviewers in understanding the candidate's strengths, weaknesses, and potential to pursue a productive career in biomedical science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter writers should follow the forthcoming instructions to provide evaluative and contextual information (strengths, weaknesses, potential) that map to the three scored criteria, helping reviewers assess preparedness, training potential, and commitment.
